title: Weeknight Beef Tacos
description: Ground beef simmered with onion, garlic, chili powder, cumin and tomato paste, spooned into warm tortillas with your choice of toppings.
scaleNote: A 12-inch skillet handles up to 2 pounds of beef. For more, brown the meat in batches so it browns instead of steaming.

image.alt: Illustration of three beef tacos with lettuce and cheese and a lime wedge on a board

steps.text: Set the skillet over medium-high heat and add the beef. Cook, breaking it into small crumbles with a spatula, until browned in spots with no pink left, {time 6-8 min}.
Tilt the pan and spoon off all but about {qty 1 tbsp} of the fat. Add the onion and cook, stirring, until softened, {time 3-4 min}.
Add the garlic, chili powder, cumin, oregano and salt and stir until fragrant, {time 30 sec}. Stir in the tomato paste and cook until it darkens slightly and coats the meat, {time 1 min}.

Pour in the water and scrape up the browned bits. Simmer, stirring now and then, until the liquid thickens and clings to the meat, {time 4-5 min}. A thermometer pushed into a mound of the meat should read at least {temp 160F internal}.

While the filling simmers, warm the tortillas one or two at a time in a dry skillet over medium-high heat until soft and lightly spotted, {time 30-60 sec} per side. Stack them in a clean kitchen towel to keep warm.
Taste the filling and add more salt if needed. Spoon it into the tortillas and top with lettuce, cheese, salsa, sour cream and cilantro, with lime wedges for squeezing.

notes: Chili powder here means the American spice blend, not pure ground chile, which is much hotter.
Ground turkey works too. It is leaner, so cook it in {qty 1 tbsp} of oil, skip spooning off the fat, and cook it to {temp 165F internal}.
Refrigerate leftover filling within 2 hours and use it within 3 days, or freeze it for up to 3 months. Reheat until steaming hot.
